cards.title: 5.1 Understanding the Natural Environment
body: Human beings exist within a specific environment, which they have modified through activities such clearing of forests, building of roads and settlements.
Ancient people had very limited effects on the natural environment.

cards.title: Worked example: cause and effect chain
cards.problem: Explain how cutting trees on a hillside can lead to flooding downstream.

steps.text: Trees and their roots hold soil and slow rain water.
Without them, rain runs off quickly and carries soil away (erosion).

cards.answer: Rivers receive more water in a short time and fill with silt, so they **flood** more easily.

questions.q: The natural environment is continuously being modified by
why: Unit 5 (Cultural impact on the physical environment) describes how overgrazing, woodcutting/deforestation, desertification and global climate change all alter the natural environment.
Every option modifies the environment. Answer: E.

questions.q: The impact of modern societies upon the natural environment is high due to
why: The textbook: 'The most significant [factors] are the growth in world population and advancement in modern technology… modern technology enables people to modify the natural environment rapidly', e.g. 'the extensive use of fossil fuel creates many types of pollution'.
B and C are consequences of the same technological way of life, but D ('lack of abundant resources') is not a cause, so 'All of the above' cannot be correct. Answer: A.
